A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeFoG and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched reliably across repagination and localized additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original DeFoG experiments on synthetic, molecular and digital pathology graphs, including quantitative benchmarks and training/sampling ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds ZINC250k molecular-generation results in Table 11.

M1.justification: The discrete flow formulation, RRWP-enhanced graph transformer, cross-entropy training, Euler sampling and distortion/guidance mechanisms are retained. Section 3.1 newly clarifies the non-edge category, without establishing a changed representation or procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds ZINC250k, containing 249,455 molecules with nine element types and up to 38 heavy atoms (Appendix F.2.2). This extends molecular-generation coverage while retaining the synthetic, QM9, MOSES, Guacamol and TLS tasks.

E2.justification: New Table 11 includes GruM, GBD and CatFlow as ZINC250k comparators. GBD is newly included; GruM and CatFlow already appear in v2 comparisons. Comparator membership in the matched existing experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added ZINC250k evaluation reports 10,000 generated graphs, 50-step and full 500-step sampling, and validity, uniqueness, FCD, NSPDK and scaffold metrics (Tables 4, 5 and 11). Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, initial-distribution tests, undertrained-model analysis, training/sampling distortion interactions and RRWP studies retain the same evidence (Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendices B, C and G.4).

E5.justification: Existing five-sampling-run and mean ± standard deviation statements are unchanged. The new ZINC250k rows also contain ± values, without specifying a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, changed run counts, seeds or statistical tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds ZINC250k results: DeFoG FCD is 1.425 ± 0.022 with full sampling and 2.123 ± 0.029 at 50 steps, versus reported FCDs of 2.257 for GruM, 2.248 for GBD and 13.211 for CatFlow. These are new benchmark results; matched existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements, assumptions, equations and proofs are retained. New Appendix D.1.3 interprets existing bounds. References such as Assumption 6 becoming Theorem 6 are inconsistent label changes, without a revised assumption or new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the claims of training/sampling decoupling, theoretical guarantees, strong graph-generation performance and efficiency using 5–10% of diffusion sampling steps. Rephrasing the first contribution bullet does not substantively change these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2.4 adds a possible mixed continuous/discrete extension and explicitly leaves it outside the evaluated scope. Appendix D.1.3 adds interpretation of the existing bounds relative to ELBO arguments, while F.3 clarifies quadratic memory scaling.

D1.justification: Tables 4–5 add ZINC250k sampler settings and resource figures, including 14 hours of training and 4.8 hours of sampling. Section 3.1 clarifies non-edge encoding, and F.3 adds memory and overhead information. Hardware and code-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds GBD, MiDi, Han et al. (2023) and Shaul et al. (2025), and expands positioning of its existing bounds relative to Campbell et al. (2022, 2024). The LSTM reference is replaced; most other bibliography edits update retained works.

P1.justification: v3 adds an appendix overview, two explanatory subsections and acknowledgements, renames theory subsections, removes duplicated dataset prose and standardizes references. Most narrative structure is retained, although several theorem/assumption cross-references become inconsistent.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 11 and ZINC250k rows to Tables 4–5, relocates Figure 13 within its explanatory section, and capitalizes MOSES in several plot titles. Other displays retain their content, with localized reflow and table renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added ZINC250k evaluation and accompanying settings provide useful extra empirical support and documentation. New scope, resource and theory-positioning discussions improve transparency. These limited gains outweigh editorial regressions, particularly references that incorrectly call the retained Assumption 6 a theorem; the core method, proofs and previous results remain unchanged.
